newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND BATSMEN TAKE COMMAND IN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-QUEENSLAND BATSMEN TAKE COMMAND IN FINAL.

text.p: Queensland made a positive start in the Sheffield Shield final on Friday after openers Trevor Barsby and Matthew Mott dominated the opening day against Western Australia.
Mott played the anchor role with an innings of 86 as Queensland reached 266 for four at close of play after winning the toss at the WACA Ground.
Barsby, playing in his last match before retiring from first-class cricket, adopted a more aggressive approach to score a rapid 67 before lunch.
Queensland captain Stuart Law, who added 115 runs for the third wicket with Mott, built on the early platform with a patient 70 against an often wayward Western Australia bowling attack.

Queensland must win in Perth to lift the Shield while a draw would be sufficient for Western Australia to take the title on the strength of their achievement in finishing top of the table at the end of the regular season.
At 227 for two, the visitors appreared to be cruising toward a massive first innings total before Mott and Law fell in quick succession after tea.
Of the top-order batsman, only number three Jimmy Maher failed to take advantage of a flat wicket ideal for batting, scoring eight runs to prolong a disappointing recent run of form.
Mott, in contrast, played with assurance during his lengthy stay at the crease, hitting six fours and one six and facing 240 balls.
The compact left-hander was finally dismissed when he struck a delivery from fast bowler Jo Angel off his pads to short mid-wicket where Ryan Campbell took a spectacular catch diving to his left.
